specificationContent.para: All avionics software shall be uniquely identified and documented according to these standards:
Software Part Numbering:
- Each software load shall have unique part number assigned by LRU manufacturer
- Part number format: [MFR_PREFIX]-[SYSTEM_CODE]-[SW_TYPE]-[VERSION]
- Example: AMPEL-31-OS-001A (AMPEL360 ATA 31 Operating System version 001A)
- Part number shall be readable from LRU without disassembly (via maintenance port, display, or label)
Software Version Documentation:
- Maintain Software Accomplishment Summary (SAS) per DO-178C for each software version
- Document design assurance level (DAL A through E) based on failure condition severity
- Include software requirements, design description, verification results, and configuration index
- Obtain regulatory authority approval for DAL A and B software changes
Software Compatibility Matrix:
- Document which software versions are compatible with specific hardware revisions
- Identify software interdependencies (e.g., display software requires specific database version)
- List approved software combinations for aircraft type certificate compliance
- Update compatibility matrix with each new software release
All software configuration changes shall follow formal change management process:
Change Request Initiation:
- Submit formal change request documenting reason for change (bug fix, enhancement, regulatory compliance)
- Include safety impact assessment and preliminary hazard analysis if applicable
- Identify affected aircraft systems and potential ripple effects
- Obtain approval from aircraft engineering authority before proceeding
Change Impact Analysis:
- Assess impact on aircraft certification basis and type certificate
- Determine if change requires supplemental type certificate (STC) or amended type certificate
- Evaluate impact on other installed systems and software versions
- Identify regression testing requirements and verification activities
Change Implementation:
- Follow DO-178C software development and verification processes for safety-critical software
- Perform requirements analysis, design, coding, and testing per approved software development plan
- Conduct software verification per Software Verification Plan (SVP)
- Document all changes in Software Configuration Management (SCM) system
Change Validation and Release:
- Complete integration testing on representative aircraft configuration
- Perform regression testing to ensure no unintended impacts
- Update Software Accomplishment Summary (SAS) with change details
- Obtain regulatory authority approval if required based on DAL and change classification
- Release software with updated part number and configuration index
Maintaining accurate records of software configuration status across aircraft fleet:
Aircraft Configuration Database:
- Maintain centralized database of software installed on each aircraft tail number
- Include LRU serial numbers, software part numbers, load dates, and installed by information
- Update database within 24 hours of any software change
- Make database accessible to maintenance planning, flight operations, and regulatory authorities
Configuration Audits:
- Conduct periodic configuration audits (quarterly or per operator requirements)
- Verify physical aircraft configuration matches database records
- Identify and correct any discrepancies found during audit
- Document audit results and corrective actions taken
Fleet Software Status Reporting:
- Generate fleet-wide software status reports showing distribution of software versions
- Identify aircraft requiring mandatory software updates per service bulletins
- Track software reliability data including fault rates and NFF rates by software version
- Provide reports to regulatory authorities as required for continued airworthiness monitoring
Formal review and approval process for software configuration changes:
CCB Membership:
- Aircraft chief engineer (chairperson)
- Software engineering representative
- Systems engineering representative
- Flight test or operations representative
- Quality assurance representative
- Certification/regulatory affairs representative
CCB Review Process:
- Review all proposed software changes for safety impact and certification compliance
- Evaluate change against aircraft design requirements and operational needs
- Assess resource requirements and schedule impact
- Approve, defer, or reject change request with documented rationale
- Assign priority and classification (critical, high, medium, low) to approved changes
CCB Meeting Frequency:
- Regular meetings: Monthly or as required by change volume
- Emergency meetings: As needed for critical safety issues or AOG situations
- Meeting minutes: Documented and archived for audit trail and regulatory compliance
